ITEM (2) -> 017.003-T: MAX_PATH threshold made UTF-16-code-unit-aware. Measured: 200 x U+00E9 = 400 UTF-8 bytes / 200 UTF-16 units; 100 x U+1F600 = 400 bytes / 200 units. UTF-8 byte length is ALWAYS >= UTF-16 code-unit count (1->1, 2->1, 3->1, 4->2), so the existing proxy fires at or before the true limit -- it can only produce a FALSE POSITIVE, never a false negative. CONFIRMED: this is a PRECISION improvement, NOT a correctness or security defect, and framing it as a vulnerability fix is an explicit anti-goal. A rune count was rejected (a surrogate pair is 1 rune but 2 UTF-16 code units, which would introduce the false negative the current code never has). The deliberation's original 'non-allocating bespoke counter' option was WITHDRAWN at plan review as gold-plating; 017.003-T uses utf16.Encode or a plain range accumulator. Plan review additionally surfaced and ACCEPTED decision D-10: dropping the \\?\ prefix in the precision-gain band re-enables ordinary Win32 normalization (trailing dot/space stripping, reserved device names CON/NUL/AUX) for those paths, which is exactly how every sub-MAX_PATH path already behaves today.
